comment: He is a good professor and cares about his students. 50% tests 50% homework. He teaches student's homework carefully, that's said, if you spend enough time, you will get 100% on the homework with his help. Test contexts are all come from his slides, if you do the practice questions, you will do well.
Don't take for macro at all costs unless you want to tank your GPA
Excel assignments were easy and he always had help sessions for them but the exams were brutal and really brought down my grade. I wish there was more extra credit opportunities.

Rating him for ECON 368 - the ETF class. Have learnt so much from his class and he really lets you do whatever you want to work on - he wants to be there to help you whatever you choose to do. If you want to be better versed in global macroeconomics and how to use that to make top-down investment decisions, definitely take his class. Free A as well

Don't take him unless you NEED to get the MACRO credit. His homework assignments are pretty easy (class average of around 94% everytime) but the part that's brutal is his exams. Fully multiple choice and rarely have anything to do with homework or lectures. Class average was around a 68%, which brought my grade down  even though I studied a ton.

Lectures can be dense because of the material, but he tries to make it engaging. Homework is easy if you go to his help sessions(which are very often.) Read the textbook as it explains the same concepts as the lectures. Overall if you put work into the class you will do fine, however, that being said the class average on tests was around 70%.

Would not recommend to anyone just taking 102 for the requirement. His class is much harder than any econ class I've taken and he expects a super deep understanding that is hard to grasp unless you are majoring in econ or super interested in it. Passionate teacher and I like how homework is 50% of your grade but test avg. were never higher than 72%

Assignments take up 50% of class while exams take up another 50%. The exams are completely multiple choice with the most random information to the point that I feel I haven't learned a single thing in class. He gives us these testbanks to study for the exams but its just 150-200 multiple choice questions per chapter that are solely based on memory.

Overall, Great Professor. However, Tests are extremely difficult and average scores are ridiculously low (about 70%). His class is way harder than years before - exams are offline, 50% scores based on assignments. Again, exams are so hard and will kill your GPA. The curve up policy remains unclear.

Professor Hayes is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. He is more than willing to stay extra hours and host multiple office hours to help students understand the material. Sadly, I think some students don't take advantage of this (in addition to not reading the textbook) and it results in their grades being poorly. All in all, great guy!

Hayes doesn't get the love he deserves. Took his ETF class but doesn't show up here so  put fin 360. He's  worked in equity research so he knows his shit. His discussions are very thought-provoking. Some students still complain about him but idk why they take this class since etf isnt part of any major. If you wanna work in finance, take him

Hayes is one of the best professors I've had. He makes his lectures and materials highly comprehensible. Exams are hard until you discover that most questions come from provided test banks. The assignments are Excel-based and challenging, but I personally found them to be very interesting and helpful. Ignore the negative reviews and just take him.

Professor Hayes was probably the worst professor I have ever taken at Richmond. His homework assignments were a large portion of the overall grade (60%) and there were around 8 of them. They used excel and he expected you to know advanced level things on excel and was extremely unhelpful when going for help. Tests were hard. Horrible professor.

In years past his tests have been online with allowed collaboration/notes with other students and this year he changed it. Same question difficulty, incredibly hard, without the extra resources. His lectures are informative but gloss over the information found on tests. Holier than thou attitude. Prepares you for an Econ102 class but not his tests.

The homework in excel is 60% of your grade (really hard so it = tons of help session) and does not relate to the test. The lecture is a waste of time and the test covers stuff that's not in the lecture. 1-hour exams have 55+ questions (tons of FRQs). In general, not the workload you'll expect from a 102 course and a big waste of time.
Just take him. Easiest Econ professor ever. All exams are online and they make 30% of your grades. The weekly assignments are 70% of your final grade. He holds sessions to help you with them.

I think Hayes is my favorite professor. His lessons are lecture heavy, but I find him very articulate and his lectures are never boring. He prints out the slides into a packet in the beginning of class, so it's easy to follow along He does weekly/biweekly assignments that are kinda fun but use excel a lot. VERY accessible outside class!

I don't see why professor Hayes is getting such low ratings. His lectures might not be the best but he explains the concepts well and is straightforward with grading criteria. The assignments are very doable so you are basically guaranteed an A even without trying hard. If you pay attention in class his does offer very useful knowledge, though.

I would not take Professor Hayes again. He was an ok professor-- teaches directly from the textbook with little synthesis. Did not enjoy his class or his demeanor. 4 tests worth 7% of your grade that are 3 hours each and open note. Very mentally draining, but I guess better than in class exams. Easy assignments though.

Professor Hayes's lectures might not be very interesting to some, but are indeed informative. He incorporates many real-life examples related to the class's content and does give thought-provoking questions. Getting an A is relatively easy if you do well on the weekly assignments (which is pretty much achievable because you can work with others).

Is there an easier econ professor you could take? Probably. There are about 12 assignments due every week and exams are open book and taken online. His assignments can be challenging and include a lot of excel, but you can work on them with people in your class and get a good grade. His lectures are boring but hw and exams are weighted the same.
Assignments Assignments and Assignments. Assignments are 75% of your grade and the tests are open book which is awesome! but the assignments are absurd.

Professor Hayes isn't the best Econ professor, but I don't think UR has any good entry level micro professors from what I've heard. The exams are open book, but they are weighted less than your weekly assignments, so even if you don't do well on them, the collaborative assignments will save you. ECON 101 is a bad class at UR, so take it elsewhere.

Class is the same every day - powerpoint lectures which are boring but informative. Gives out 8-10 moderately easy assignments which come directly from the lectures and sometimes offers extra credit opportunities. He worked in corporate before teaching so he focuses a lot more on applications and spreadsheets rather than theoretical concepts.
Good professor and makes lectures bearable. Always available to help with the assignments which is useful since they are the majority of your grade.

Professor Hayes knows what he's talking about. He says to buy the textbook but you definitely don't NEED it. However, you need the access to the online site as that is where tests are. You have unlimited time to take them and most of your grade (70%) is based off of assignments which are collaborative and pretty easy.

Hayes is a great professor! Hands out notes (PPs) before class, but you should read. Really great at explaining - easy to understand. 10 assignments, which weren't bad; just ask questions if you don't understand. No hw besides reading. Also, he's really funny, but in an unintentional kind of way! I'm ngl, I had a crush on him, thank god for masks!

Prof. Hayes has a knack for teaching concepts in a simple and memorable manner. He is a always available for consultation outside of class, and he gives up his time to have study sessions with students, even on the weekends. You can consult him for anything even if it is not pertinent to coursework; if he can help, he will.

Hayes' class is very lecture-heavy. Overall though, I think he's a great teacher. It's tough to make ANY lecture interesting and he's usually very enthusiastic and does a good job. He sends out test banks which help greatly with the tests and there were about 4-5 doable assignments that we had to complete. (Big excel guy) Also surprisingly funny.

Provides binder with lecture slides to take notes on during the lectures. Be sure to carefully follow the instructions for the assignments and study the test banks and articles for the tests. Overall a good experience.

Very underwhelming professor who struggles to teach the material in a way that is engaging or interesting. Homeworks have little connection to lecture material, and do not improve your understanding of concepts.

His class is around 8 assignments and 4 tests. The tests are difficult but he gives test banks and if you study them hard you'll be fine. Class is all lectures which can get pretty boring, but you should pay attention to do well on the tests. His assignments are longer HWs and aren't too bad, if you follow instructions you can get As on em.

Professor Hayes is the GOAT. Do the homework assignments and put a ton of effort into them with a lot of attention to detail. Don't need the textbook just do the test banks before the tests, material is pretty straight forward from the lectures.

Professor Hayes is a very very good lecturer and teaches the material clearly. However, he grades extremely harshly and takes off a lot of points for extremely small mistakes. The tests are copied from the test banks he posts online but the test banks are hundreds of questions long, so it's nearly impossible to practice all the questions.

Would not take again. Somehow makes finance a subjective class. Lectures are extremely boring and he simply reads off of powerpoint slides. It's a better use of your time to not show up and just read the textbook.

He is a decent professor, gives like ten assignments per semester to grade. The assignments can get tricky and takes time, however, his in class tests aren't hard. He provides practice questions that are very similar to his tests. You can just go and listen him in-class since he provides you the class notes which saves so much of your time.

The lectures can get really boring, but he is a decent prof. No homework, only a few tests, one essay, and an excel project. The in class tests are literally copied from the test banks, so just study the test banks and you will be fine. The take home tests can be tricky. Good teacher, not very exciting, but he gets the job done.

Professor Hayes is an ok professor. He uses a lot of real world examples in his lectures, however they are often longwinded and can get boring. The in class tests are not to difficult, but If you are not an expert you will not get As on take home tests. Also one extremely difficult excel project. Overall not the hardest class, but not an easy  A

The in-class tests are pretty easy if you do the test banks, but those take a lot of time so do them early. The take home portions are absolutely impossible and he grades them really hard. The material found on the take home cannot even be found in the book. There is also a project at the end of the semester that is incredibly hard.

One of the few professors I really like! Look forward to his lectures- he is very clear, takes time to make sure students understand the concepts, and very helpful outside of class. He provides you with test banks and if you study those questions you will do fine on the in-class tests. Take-home tests are a bit tricky but not too bad!

Nice man and cares about his students. Clear lectures, explanations, grading. Very fair grader but it is important to show up and work hard. Seems like he'd be a bro outside of class. Was very helpful outside of class. when I needed assistance on a project.

Makes it very clear what's expected of you. Straightforward approach to economics, understand the textbook and you'll succeed. Very helpful during office hours and more than willing to help students during test cram sessions (which are super helpful).

A total of three tests. 50% in class and 50% take home and a cumulative final. Had a super easy project. He's usually clear, but sometimes he's confusing.  Would take again. You should attend the class though.
